items.streamTitle: Eye-tracking BIDS standard specifies gaze, pupil and asynchronous event data
items.streamSummary: A November 27 BIDS extension standardizes eye-tracking data, pupil measurements and asynchronous event metadata to support reproducible research.
items.attribution: Szinte, Bach, Draschkow et al. — Scientific Data (technical standard; November 27, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Workplace incivility was associated with cynicism through two distinct perceptions
items.streamSummary: A two-wave survey of 429 Chinese service workers linked incivility with cynicism through two modeled pathways; ethical climate moderated first-stage associations but not the full indirect effects.
items.attribution: Qiu, Li and Choi — Frontiers in Psychology (observational survey; November 26, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Research-agent benchmark measured improvements over established expert solutions
items.streamSummary: REE tested four agents on 100 expert-reviewed research problems; two surpassed expert-solution scores on 86% and 81% of tasks. The benchmark does not establish autonomous scientific discovery.
items.attribution: Zhou, Liu, Liu et al. — arXiv preprint (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Actor-aware permutation tests improved inference for network interaction counts
items.streamSummary: A Poisson network-regression preprint shows how actor effects and dependence-aware permutations can control false positives in simulated interaction-count networks.
items.attribution: Dekker and Krause — arXiv preprint (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Cross-lagged model comparisons explain how apparent relationships can reverse
items.streamSummary: A theoretical preprint derives identification conditions for random-intercept panel models and shows when conventional lagged coefficients may reverse or cancel.
items.attribution: Cao — arXiv preprint (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: NATO exercise integrates civilian organizations into multinational crisis training
items.streamSummary: NATO's November 25 exercise announcement documents civil-military participation and new exercise-content tools; measured readiness or coordination outcomes have not been reported.
items.attribution: NATO Joint Warfare Centre — official exercise announcement (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Distributed AI teams lost essential information despite collectively possessing it
items.streamSummary: Controlled AI experiments distinguished losses caused by insufficient messages from failures to select or use available evidence. More interaction was not always necessary.
items.attribution: Chu and Shen — arXiv preprint (November 24, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Loneliness was associated with divergent neural segmentation of shared events
items.streamSummary: Two fMRI datasets linked loneliness to less shared neural event segmentation during video viewing; the direction of causality remains unknown.
items.attribution: Lu, Sava-Segal and Baek — Communications Psychology (November 26, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Digital persuasion commentary distinguishes exposure from per-person effects
items.streamSummary: A conceptual commentary argues that population-level media effects depend on both reach and per-person response, and that exposure variation may dominate. It reports no new campaign trial.
items.attribution: Ben M. Tappin — Nature Human Behaviour (commentary; November 26, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Neural decoding methods exposed leakage from preprocessing and random time-series splits
items.streamSummary: Neural decoding analysis showed that preprocessing leakage can bias performance in either direction and random folds can overstate accuracy for dependent time series.
items.attribution: Wong, McCullough, Lu et al. — Nature Communications (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Social feedback surprises were linked to greater self-esteem reactivity in adolescence
items.streamSummary: An experiment and daily-life sampling of 141 people linked age to self-esteem responses to unexpected social feedback; the laboratory and daily-life age patterns differed.
items.attribution: Gregorova, Will, Burkard et al. — Nature Communications (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Fifty-five randomized designs found small shifts in carbon-pricing support
items.streamSummary: A 19,558-person many-designs experiment found small average changes in carbon-pricing support across 55 trials, below researchers' expectations.
items.attribution: Holzknecht, Schwaiger, Blanco et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (November 25, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Open video-emotion dataset pairs neural signals with granular human ratings
items.streamSummary: A public MEG/video dataset includes 23 recorded participants, 40 clips and survey validation in 500 respondents; reported classification concerns stimulus categories.
items.attribution: Yoo, Kim, Choi et al. — Scientific Data (November 14, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Research agents struggled to honor prior decisions in real project workspaces
items.streamSummary: ARE-bench found that judging deliverables alone substantially overstated research-agent success when historical and workspace requirements were omitted.
items.attribution: Lin, Ren, Xu et al. — arXiv preprint (November 10, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Planning agents frequently missed facts needed to construct feasible plans
items.streamSummary: Ask2Decide found large feasibility losses when AI planners lacked facts, and substantial differences between human and uncalibrated simulated operator replies.
items.attribution: Tang, Fan, Zou et al. — arXiv preprint (November 9, 2026; revised November 15)

items.streamTitle: NATO issued public-private resilience cooperation guidance
items.streamSummary: NATO announced public-private resilience guidance on November 24, emphasizing joint planning and exercises to sustain essential services. Readiness gains were not measured.
items.attribution: NATO — official Resilience Symposium announcement (November 24, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Reward changed visual search strategy more than processing speed
items.streamSummary: A randomized visual-search study found faster searches and fewer fixations under reward, without a significant accuracy difference. Strategy changes explained more of the advantage than faster within-fixation processing.
items.attribution: Shdeour and Yuval-Greenberg — Scientific Reports (randomized eye-tracking experiment; November 24, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Incivility correlated with delayed action in real crisis teams
items.streamSummary: Real trauma-team observations associated incivility with slower diagnostic action and patient pain; information seeking moderated one association. No causal intervention was tested.
items.attribution: Lim, Goh, Tay et al. — Scientific Reports (naturalistic crisis-team field study; November 24, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Causal triangulation framework separated target differences from assumption failures
items.streamSummary: A formal triangulation framework distinguishes differences in causal targets from identification discrepancies and explains why agreement cannot eliminate shared bias.
items.attribution: García Meixide and Ríos Insua — arXiv preprint (causal identification methodology; November 23, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Interpretable subgroup discovery extended causal modeling to continuous treatment doses
items.streamSummary: A new recursive partitioning method discovers heterogeneous causal dose-response curves with subgroup-specific estimation. Behavioral applications remain untested.
items.attribution: Bargagli-Stoffi, Pham, Kennedy et al. — arXiv preprint (causal estimation methods; November 23, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Brain encoding models generalized meaning across 21 languages
items.streamSummary: Human fMRI encoding models generalized to unseen languages across 21 languages, supporting a shared semantic component. This does not demonstrate uniform cross-cultural interpretation or persuasion.
items.attribution: de Varda, Malik-Moraleda, Tuckute et al. — Nature Neuroscience (cross-language fMRI encoding study; November 23, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Changing numerical rating scales shifted AI judge scores
items.streamSummary: An LLM-judge benchmark found scale width and placement changed scores and calibration even without changing the evaluated content. Larger judges were generally more robust.
items.attribution: Kim, Kim, Kum, Song and Park — arXiv preprint (November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Synchronized smartphone-use dataset combines gaze and physiological signals
items.streamSummary: A public dataset aligns EEG, gaze and physiological recordings during smartphone use in 30 people. It enables multimodal attention research, not causal conclusions about media effects.
items.attribution: Mishra, Gandhi and Gandhi — Scientific Data (data descriptor; November 11, 2026)

items.streamTitle: AI impact review finds limited evidence for strongest claims of harm
items.streamSummary: A peer-reviewed review of eight AI impact domains finds limited support for the strongest harm claims, with substantial unresolved uncertainty and heterogeneous evidence.
items.attribution: Summerfield, Anselmetti, Avin et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (review; November 24, 2026)
